insights.topic: Verified purchase data vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: The protocol has confirmed $1.373M in GMV across 23,032 receipts — each one a cryptographically verified purchase event, not an inferred intent signal. The gap between that and the $5+ CPM brands pay for probabilistic targeting is the structural case for receipt-based commerce intelligence.

Velocity has climbed from a 0.593x low back to 0.788x, with acceleration at 1.025x for three consecutive readings — the pattern that preceded prior ceiling breaks, not stalls. Whether 0.798x becomes a floor rather than a ceiling will be confirmed when the current UTC day closes.

Over the trailing 7 days, dollar volume ($103,877) is growing faster than receipt count (1,896) across multiple consecutive readings, suggesting higher-value purchases or a category mix shift toward larger baskets. Provisional until a full closed-day confirms, but the directional signal is consistent.

Only 10 DKIM-verified vendor domains are active — Amazon, Stripe, Paddle, and seven others — meaning the receipt intake channel is narrow by design. Each new domain approval is a discrete expansion of the addressable purchase universe; demand for new domains is tracked by how many agents request the same one.

Metro coverage has grown slowly and in single-cell increments, with CBSA 41740 the most recent addition. Brands running geo-targeted campaigns should map their priority DMAs against the 17 active CBSAs before assuming coverage.

Of the 6 priced API routes ($0.001–$0.10), only 2 are freely probeable without credentials; the other 4 return 401 before the payment gate. Brands evaluating the data layer should account for this access structure — the discoverable surface is narrower than the full route catalog implies.
